lesson_title: The Circular Flow: Leakages and Injections
hook_text: Your R500 in savings just left the economy. Here's how it sneaks back in.
clip_script: Suppose households save part of their income at the bank. That money leaves the spending stream — it is income earned but not passed back to firms. We call any such escape a leakage. Savings is our first leakage. Does saved money vanish? No — and this is the beautiful part. Banks and other financial institutions lend those savings to firms, which use them to buy machinery, buildings and equipment. That spending on capital goods is called investment, and it pumps money back into the flow. Any such re-entry is called an injection. Savings leak out; investment injects back in — connected through the financial sector.
visual_style: Glowing circular pipeline of money with animated leaks dripping out and syringes injecting flow back in, labels appearing as each term lands.
pacing: Fast hook, steady middle as the loop builds, snappy payoff on 'injection'.
